title: Who he is
text: Asadullah Faisal (also called Faizal). AI & Data Science · IIT Jodhpur. I'm a final-year AI & Data Science student at IIT Jodhpur. I build machine learning systems and then measure where they break: a text detector for Indian street signs, an LLM agent that cannot act without permission, and the benchmarks that keep both honest.

title: Research overview
text: Asadullah Faisal's research: Scene text detection in Indian languages. B.Tech Project with Prof. Anand Mishra, IIT Jodhpur, since August 2026 (ongoing). B.Tech research on finding text in Indian street photos: auditing the TextBPN++ detector, fixing a preprocessing mismatch, and fine-tuning faster detectors on the Bharat Scene Text Dataset.

title: Research problem
text: The problem in Asadullah Faisal's research: The Bharat Scene Text Dataset's 1,319 test images are high resolution. Once resized for a detector, small words shrink to a few pixels and get missed, and very large words break the detector too.

title: Research: Audit
text: In his research, Asadullah Faisal — Audit: Reproduced and audited the TextBPN++ detector on all 1,319 test images. Built a polygon-IoU evaluation harness with per-image error logs and text-size stratification, which exposed a recall collapse on small text (under 20 px: recall 0.35) and on very large text (over 320 px).

title: Research: Preprocessing fix
text: In his research, Asadullah Faisal — Preprocessing fix: Traced a train/inference preprocessing mismatch: inference skipped the mean/std normalization the model was trained with. Fixing it raised detection recall from 0.621 to 0.670 and F1 from 0.656 to 0.675, without retraining.

title: Research: Small text
text: In his research, Asadullah Faisal — Small text: Scale-aware 1.5× upscaling lifted small-text F1 from 0.47 to 0.59. Tiled inference was tested and rejected: it added 67 false positives for 4 true positives.

title: Research: Fine-tuning
text: In his research, Asadullah Faisal — Fine-tuning: Fine-tuned YOLO11, docTR FAST and DPText-DETR on 4.7K training images, with polygon-to-box conversion, EXIF and coordinate correction, and a leak-free 90/10 split (test set held out). The fine-tuned YOLO raised end-to-end OCR word recall from 50.7% to 54.3% and F1 from 51.0% to 53.8%. It is now the toolkit fork's default detector (5.5 MB, release yolo11n-bstd-v1.0).

title: Research: Benchmark
text: In his research, Asadullah Faisal — Benchmark: Benchmarked 10 text detectors (EAST, CRAFT, DBNet++ and others) and IoU-based polygon-fusion ensembles to map the precision–recall trade-off. A 5-model ensemble reached recall 56.7% but precision only 40.3%.

title: Research results: TextBPN++ detection on the BSTD test set, before and after fixing the preprocessing mismatch (no retraining)
text: Asadullah Faisal's research result. TextBPN++ detection on the BSTD test set, before and after fixing the preprocessing mismatch (no retraining): Setup As shipped, Recall 0.621, F1 0.656; Setup Normalization fixed, Recall 0.670, F1 0.675.

title: Research results: Small-text F1
text: Asadullah Faisal's research result. Small-text F1: Setup Baseline, Small-text F1 0.47; Setup Scale-aware 1.5× upscaling, Small-text F1 0.59. Tiled inference was rejected: +67 false positives for +4 true positives.

title: Research results: End-to-end OCR (detection → script identification → PARSeq recognition)
text: Asadullah Faisal's research result. End-to-end OCR (detection → script identification → PARSeq recognition): Detector Before fine-tuning, Word recall 50.7%, F1 51.0%; Detector Fine-tuned YOLO, Word recall 54.3%, F1 53.8%.

text: Asadullah Faisal's research result. Precision–recall trade-off of a 5-model polygon-fusion ensemble: Setup 5-model ensemble, Recall 56.7%, Precision 40.3%. Ensembling buys recall at a steep cost in precision.

title: Project: OpsPilot
text: Asadullah Faisal's project OpsPilot: An AI operations assistant that investigates incidents with evidence, but can only act through a server-side policy engine, human approval and verified execution. Problem it addresses: An LLM agent that can restart services or roll back deployments is dangerous if the model decides what is safe. OpsPilot keeps the model in charge of investigating and the server in charge of permission.

title: OpsPilot: what he built
text: In OpsPilot, Asadullah Faisal built: An agent loop with 6 typed, read-only tools (service health, metrics, log search, recent deployments, incident history, runbook search) over a simulated production environment. The model chooses which tools to call; the tools themselves are deterministic.

title: OpsPilot: what he built
text: In OpsPilot, Asadullah Faisal built: Hybrid retrieval over runbooks and postmortems in PostgreSQL + pgvector: 128-dimension hashed bag-of-words vectors plus a keyword score. No learned embedding model, by design (ADR-0002).

title: OpsPilot: what he built
text: In OpsPilot, Asadullah Faisal built: Competing hypotheses, each with supporting and contradicting evidence, before a fix is proposed.

title: OpsPilot: what he built
text: In OpsPilot, Asadullah Faisal built: A server-side policy engine (role × risk × environment). Risk comes from a server table, never from the model, so a spoofed 'LOW risk' claim cannot bypass it.

title: OpsPilot: what he built
text: In OpsPilot, Asadullah Faisal built: Durable human approval, simulator execution, a verification step (SUCCESS / FAILED / INCONCLUSIVE), and append-only audit and agent-event tables enforced by database triggers.

title: OpsPilot: what he built
text: In OpsPilot, Asadullah Faisal built: 116 pytest tests, including prompt-injection and approval-bypass suites.

title: OpsPilot: what he built
text: In OpsPilot, Asadullah Faisal built: OpsBench 2.0.0: 100 scenarios across 12 categories, including prompt injection, misleading evidence and permission violations.

title: OpsPilot: results
text: OpsPilot results. OpsBench 2.0.0, Groq openai/gpt-oss-120b, temperature 0. Source: backend/benchmarks/opsbench/v2/results/summary.md: System Plain LLM baseline, Task success 24%, Diagnosis 3%, Safety 26%; System OpsPilot (run 1), Task success 69%, Diagnosis 69%, Safety 86%; System OpsPilot (run 2), Task success 71%, Diagnosis 72%, Safety 86%.

title: OpsPilot: finding
text: OpsPilot finding: Removing verification: 17 incidents marked resolved while the fault remained (0 with it).

title: OpsPilot: finding
text: OpsPilot finding: Removing retrieval: diagnosis fell from 69% to 44%.

title: OpsPilot: finding
text: OpsPilot finding: A fixed investigation plan beat free planning: 81% task success and 97% safety with about 4× fewer tokens.

title: OpsPilot: finding
text: OpsPilot finding: Misleading-evidence scenarios: 0/8. The agent still falls for planted evidence.

title: OpsPilot: caveats
text: OpsPilot caveats: I wrote both the scenarios and the labels. Diagnosis and grounding are scored by term matching. The simulated reviewer approves unless a scenario says to reject. One scenario per run was rerun after network errors.

text: OpsPilot tech stack: Next.js 14, TypeScript, FastAPI, PostgreSQL 16 + pgvector, Groq (openai/gpt-oss-120b), Gemini (supported, not benchmarked), JWT, Docker, pytest.

title: Project: semantic-hire
text: Asadullah Faisal's project semantic-hire: Ranks job descriptions against a resume by meaning plus verified skill overlap, with an LLM allowed to explain results but never to rank them. Problem it addresses: Keyword matching misses resumes that describe the right work in different words; pure embeddings ignore hard skill requirements.

title: semantic-hire: what he built
text: In semantic-hire, Asadullah Faisal built: Embeds jobs (title + description + skills) and resumes with all-MiniLM-L6-v2, normalized, retrieved with an exact FAISS IndexFlatIP.

title: semantic-hire: what he built
text: In semantic-hire, Asadullah Faisal built: Re-ranks the retrieved jobs by 0.7 × semantic score + 0.3 × skill overlap, where overlap is the share of the job's skills found in the resume.

title: semantic-hire: what he built
text: In semantic-hire, Asadullah Faisal built: Dictionary-based skill extraction (49 skills) with boundary-aware matching, so 'Java' does not match inside 'JavaScript'.

title: semantic-hire: what he built
text: In semantic-hire, Asadullah Faisal built: Optional Gemini explanation after ranking, validated so it can only cite skills the matcher actually verified. If Gemini fails, ranked results still return.

title: semantic-hire: what he built
text: In semantic-hire, Asadullah Faisal built: Evaluation with Precision@K, Recall@K, MRR and NDCG@K on a hand-labelled query set.

title: semantic-hire: results
text: semantic-hire results. 8 hand-labelled queries over 24 synthetic job descriptions, K = 5. Source: evaluation/results.json: Precision@5 0.650, Recall@5 0.881, MRR 1.000, NDCG@5 0.901.

title: semantic-hire: caveats
text: semantic-hire caveats: A demonstration benchmark, not an estimate of production quality: 24 jobs and 8 queries, all written by me. Three queries have only 3 relevant jobs, so their Precision@5 cannot exceed 0.6.

title: semantic-hire: tech stack
text: semantic-hire tech stack: Python, sentence-transformers, FAISS, FastAPI, Gemini (google-genai), Docker, pytest.

text: semantic-hire source code: https://github.com/Asadalk/semantic-hire

title: Project: SmokeTrail
text: Asadullah Faisal's project SmokeTrail (in progress): Do upwind crop fires in Punjab and Haryana show up in Delhi's air the next day? A classical data science study, no LLMs. Problem it addresses: Every autumn, crop-residue fires in Punjab and Haryana coincide with Delhi's worst air. The question: how much higher is Delhi's daily PM2.5 on days with heavy upwind burning, after adjusting for weather, and can today's fires predict tomorrow's air?

title: SmokeTrail: plan
text: Planned for SmokeTrail: Data: Kaggle 'Air Quality Data in India' (city_day), NASA FIRMS VIIRS fire detections, Open-Meteo historical weather. Sep 15 – Dec 15, 2015–2019.

title: SmokeTrail: plan
text: Planned for SmokeTrail: Upwind-fire feature: fires inside a ±30° cone around the wind direction, 1–3 day lags, fires within 50 km of Delhi excluded.

title: SmokeTrail: plan
text: Planned for SmokeTrail: OLS with robustness checks and a placebo test; LightGBM + SHAP forecasting with train 2015–17 / validate 2018 / test 2019.

title: SmokeTrail: plan
text: Planned for SmokeTrail: Dashboard: Streamlit + pydeck (planned).

title: SmokeTrail: status
text: SmokeTrail status: Project setup is done; data collection and modelling are under way. Results will appear here only once the code produces them.

title: Project: Cellular Network Metadata Processing System
text: Asadullah Faisal's project Cellular Network Metadata Processing System: An Android app reads the phone's serving cell (LTE or 5G NR), a FastAPI service looks it up in PostgreSQL, and the tower location appears on an OpenStreetMap map. Problem it addresses: Show, end to end and explainably, how a phone's cell identity (MCC, MNC, TAC, CID) becomes an approximate location, without pretending to more precision than the data allows.

title: Cellular Network Metadata Processing System: what he built
text: In Cellular Network Metadata Processing System, Asadullah Faisal built: Kotlin Android client that reads the registered serving cell for LTE (CellInfoLte) and 5G NR (CellInfoNr, NCI as cell ID), handling Android API-level differences.

title: Cellular Network Metadata Processing System: what he built
text: In Cellular Network Metadata Processing System, Asadullah Faisal built: Retrofit 2.9 client posting the cell identity to a FastAPI /locate endpoint.

title: Cellular Network Metadata Processing System: what he built
text: In Cellular Network Metadata Processing System, Asadullah Faisal built: Exact-match lookup in PostgreSQL over Indian tower data (MCC 404/405) from a Kaggle dataset derived from OpenCellID.

title: Cellular Network Metadata Processing System: what he built
text: In Cellular Network Metadata Processing System, Asadullah Faisal built: osmdroid map with a marker and a fixed 1,000 m circle, deliberately not triangulated, to avoid false precision.
